cpi.name: CPI Retail Inflation
cpi.plainEnglishDefinition: Measures how fast everyday household prices (groceries, rent, fuel, healthcare, and education) are rising compared to one year ago.
cpi.whyItMatters: The Reserve Bank of India aims to keep retail inflation inside a 2% to 6% comfort band (targeting 4%). Because prices usually surge only after strong demand has been running for a while, inflation acts like a rearview mirror confirming an overheating boom.
cpi.exampleGeneric: When retail inflation is high, the same monthly basket of groceries, rent, school fees and medicines costs noticeably more than it did a year ago, so household savings shrink unless salaries rise as fast.

wpi.name: WPI Wholesale Inflation
wpi.plainEnglishDefinition: Tracks bulk prices paid by factories, distributors, and wholesalers for raw materials, fuel, power, and manufactured goods before items reach retail shops.
wpi.whyItMatters: When factory input and energy costs jump for several months in a row, companies face squeezed profits and eventually pass those higher costs on to regular shoppers.
wpi.exampleGeneric: Wholesale prices are what shops and factories pay. When diesel, steel or cooking oil gets dearer at the wholesale level, shop prices for those items usually rise a few weeks later.

unemployment.name: Unemployment Rate (PLFS)
unemployment.plainEnglishDefinition: Shows the percentage of people actively looking for work who do not currently have a job.
unemployment.whyItMatters: Hiring and training workers is expensive, so companies only expand headcount aggressively once they are confident business growth is real. Falling unemployment confirms a healthy expansion has been underway.
unemployment.exampleGeneric: A falling unemployment rate means more people looking for work find it, so fresh graduates get offers sooner and workers have more power to ask for a raise.

bank_credit.name: Bank Credit Growth
bank_credit.plainEnglishDefinition: Measures how fast Indian banks are giving out new loans to families (home, car, personal loans) and businesses compared to a year ago.
bank_credit.whyItMatters: Healthy loan growth (around 12% to 16%) fuels business expansion. However, when lending grows much faster than bank deposits for months, banks stretch their funding and credit booms can eventually trigger overheating.
bank_credit.exampleGeneric: Fast credit growth means banks are lending freely for homes, cars and businesses. It helps growth, but very fast lending can push up prices and risky loans.

repo_rate.name: RBI Repo Rate (Policy Rate)
repo_rate.plainEnglishDefinition: The benchmark interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term money to commercial banks.
repo_rate.whyItMatters: Central banks raise the repo rate to cool down fast-rising prices and slow excessive borrowing. Starting a rate-hike cycle is a classic late-stage boom signal.
repo_rate.exampleGeneric: The repo rate sets the base for loan rates. When RBI raises it, EMIs on new and floating-rate home and car loans usually go up within a few months; when it cuts, they go down.

core_industries.name: Index of Core Industries (ICI)
core_industries.plainEnglishDefinition: Tracks the real-time production of India's 8 backbone industries: electricity, steel, refinery products, crude oil, coal, cement, natural gas, and fertilizers.
core_industries.whyItMatters: These 8 sectors make up roughly 40% of India's industrial output. Because you cannot build highways, homes, or power factories without steel, cement, and electricity, this is a reliable live speedometer.
core_industries.exampleGeneric: Coal, electricity, steel, cement and fuel feed almost every other industry. When their output grows, it usually means construction sites, factories and power plants are busy.

iip.name: Index of Industrial Production (IIP)
iip.plainEnglishDefinition: Measures total physical production volume across Indian factories, mines, and electricity utilities compared to the same month last year.
iip.whyItMatters: Factory production rises and falls right in sync with the broader economy, giving a much faster monthly read than quarterly GDP numbers.
iip.exampleGeneric: Factory output covers everything from cars to medicines. Rising output means more shifts, more overtime and steadier jobs for factory workers.

rail_freight.name: Railway Freight Loading
rail_freight.plainEnglishDefinition: The weight of goods that Indian Railways carries in a month, such as coal, iron ore, cement, food grains and containers, compared with the same month one year ago.
rail_freight.whyItMatters: Factories, power plants and traders move most bulk goods by rail. When more goods move, more is being produced and sold right now. Freight data comes out within days of the month ending, so it shows current activity sooner than most official statistics.
rail_freight.exampleGeneric: When a steel plant in Odisha gets more orders, it books more rakes of iron ore and coal. That extra loading shows up in the railway freight number weeks before it shows up in factory output data.

gst.name: GST Collections
gst.plainEnglishDefinition: The total Goods and Services Tax collected across India each month whenever businesses sell products or services.
gst.whyItMatters: Because GST is billed on almost every formal sale from restaurant meals to factory shipments, it acts as a live nationwide cash-register reading of consumer and business spending.
gst.exampleGeneric: GST is paid on most things people buy. Higher collections mean more buying and selling across the country, and more money for the government to spend on roads and schemes.

vehicles.name: Passenger Vehicle Sales
vehicles.plainEnglishDefinition: Counts how many new cars, SUVs, and vans automakers shipped to Indian dealerships during the month.
vehicles.whyItMatters: Buying a car is one of the biggest discretionary purchases a household makes. Families only commit to multi-year car loans when they feel secure about their jobs and incomes.
vehicles.exampleGeneric: Car and SUV sales show how confident families feel about big purchases. Strong sales usually mean steady incomes and easy loan approvals.

gdp.name: Real GDP Growth (Reference)
gdp.plainEnglishDefinition: The broadest scorecard of the entire economy, measuring the inflation-adjusted value of all goods and services produced in India over a quarter.
gdp.whyItMatters: Real GDP is the official benchmark of economic expansion. India's long-term normal trend is about 6.5% to 7.0% a year. Growth above that range means the economy is running above normal capacity; growth below it means spare capacity.
gdp.exampleGeneric: GDP growth is the total of all incomes earned in the country. Faster growth usually means more jobs, more business for shops and higher tax collections.

nifty.name: Nifty 50 (Stock Market)
nifty.plainEnglishDefinition: The closing value of the Nifty 50, an index of 50 large companies listed on the National Stock Exchange, as republished by the Reserve Bank of India.
nifty.whyItMatters: Share prices react to what investors expect for company profits in the coming months. A steady rise often comes before stronger business activity; a sharp fall often comes before a slowdown. One day's move means little, so the signal looks at the change over about three months.
nifty.exampleGeneric: If you put a fixed amount into an index fund every month through a SIP, your fund tracks this index. A rising Nifty lifts the value of those savings; a falling Nifty lowers it.

yield_spread.name: Bond Yield Spread (10Y vs Repo)
yield_spread.plainEnglishDefinition: The gap between what the Indian government pays to borrow for 10 years versus short-term borrowing rates (100 bps equals 1%).
yield_spread.whyItMatters: Normally, long-term interest rates sit comfortably above short-term rates. When that gap shrinks to zero or flips negative (called an inversion), bond markets are warning that a slowdown is approaching.
yield_spread.exampleGeneric: When long-term government bonds pay clearly more than the repo rate, lenders expect normal growth ahead. If the gap closes or turns negative, markets expect a slowdown.

consumer_confidence.name: Consumer Confidence (RBI)
consumer_confidence.plainEnglishDefinition: The Reserve Bank of India's Future Expectations Index: how households in 19 cities expect the economy, jobs, prices, their income and their spending to change over the next year. Above 100 means more optimists than pessimists.
consumer_confidence.whyItMatters: Household spending is more than half of India's economy. When families expect better incomes and jobs, they buy more homes, vehicles and appliances in the months that follow. The index is computed as 100 plus the average of five net responses, the formula RBI publishes with the survey.
consumer_confidence.exampleGeneric: A family in Pune that expects a salary rise next year is more likely to book a new two-wheeler or start home renovation now. Many such decisions together move this index.

industrial_outlook.name: Business Expectations (RBI)
industrial_outlook.plainEnglishDefinition: The Reserve Bank of India's Business Expectations Index: how manufacturing companies expect production, orders, jobs and profits to change in the next quarter. Above 100 means more companies expect improvement than decline.
industrial_outlook.whyItMatters: Companies plan production, hiring and investment on what they expect, not on last month's results. Their expectations often turn before actual output does, which makes this a leading signal.
industrial_outlook.exampleGeneric: When a textile mill in Tiruppur expects more export orders next quarter, it hires workers and buys yarn now. RBI's survey asks companies like this about their plans.

oecd_cli.name: OECD Leading Index (CLI)
oecd_cli.plainEnglishDefinition: An international forward-looking indicator built to spot economic turning points 6 to 9 months ahead. A reading of 100 represents India's long-term normal trend.
oecd_cli.whyItMatters: When the index sits above 100 and keeps ticking higher, it signals the economy is expanding above its normal pace with no broad downturn in sight yet.
oecd_cli.exampleGeneric: The OECD's leading index combines several early signals into one number. Above 100 means activity is above its long-term trend; the direction shows where it is heading.
